objective: Correct DR24 workspace session ownership and retention, strengthen browser acceptance coverage, and define an evidence-based desktop UI framework evaluation without changing the scientific core.

previous_knowledge_consumed.source: Issue #324 — DR24 session loss across menu navigation
previous_knowledge_consumed.detail: Workspace navigation must preserve OID draft, successful payload, rendered records, provenance and export state within the same process.
Review identified an in-flight response workspace-isolation defect and stale rendered state after export restoration.
WebView-based desktop UI and Python local API are the current implementation; Preview 5 must remain unchanged.
Architecture, backend, QA, UX, release and independent red-team roles must challenge assumptions; project owner retains final approval.

correctness.before: DR24 navigation acceptance failed on an immediate post-navigation assertion; review found request results could be written to a newly active workspace.
correctness.after: Workspace-bound request handling and asynchronous UI wait assertions added; exact-head browser result pending.

reliability.before: A failed subsequent request could replace visible state; restored exports could leave stale rendered markup.
reliability.after: Retain last successful payload and export; clear stale rendering on export restoration; exact-head verification pending.

reproducibility.reason: No exact-head workflow result is available for this cycle yet.

memory.reason: No controlled Qt versus WebView2 prototype measurements have been collected.

latency.reason: No comparative application startup-latency benchmark has been collected.

measurement.trade_off: Keep WebView2 operational. Qt Quick/QML remains a prototype candidate. Do not add Qt or .NET production dependencies or change scientific behavior.

evidence: PR #325 review identified two correctness risks: late DR24 responses can target the wrong workspace, and restored exports can retain stale rendered markup.
The branch now captures the request's originating workspace session and only updates visible state when that workspace remains active.
The branch now retains the last successful result and export after a failed later acquisition.
The branch now resets rendered state and records provenance/status when restoring a saved raw export.
Browser acceptance coverage now includes delayed in-flight workspace switching and failed-request retention.
Navigation tests now wait for asynchronous workspace restoration before checking the input state.
Desktop UI framework evaluation document records the current WebView2 baseline, Qt Quick/QML prototype path, and why WPF is not the primary multi-platform path.

root_causes: The asynchronous DR24 response path previously wrote to module-level state that could point to a different workspace after awaits.
Export restoration replaced payload and OIDs but did not replace the rendered result markup or provenance/status.
The browser acceptance test asserted restored OID state immediately after a navigation click, before the asynchronous active-workspace lookup had completed.

findings: Every asynchronous scientific acquisition must capture its workspace identity and session before network awaits.
A response may update the visible page only when its originating workspace is still active; otherwise it may update only its captured workspace session.
A failed later acquisition must not overwrite the last successful result or export.
Restored raw exports must not be paired with stale plots or stale provenance.
UI tests must wait for asynchronous view restoration before asserting state.
A UI framework replacement is not a root-cause fix for state-management defects.
Qt Quick/QML should be evaluated through a bounded, API-backed prototype; no migration decision is justified without cross-platform and resource measurements.

open_blockers: Run the focused DR24 browser contract on the latest branch head, including retention of OID draft 707 when its request is in flight during a workspace switch.
Run the full CI workflow, including the cumulative lifecycle gate and test suite.
Run Windows desktop runtime, installer, install/launch/uninstall acceptance on the exact branch head.
Verify in-flight workspace isolation, export restoration, failed-request retention, no duplicate acquisition, and same-process workspace restoration.
Review all new code and test results before marking PR #325 ready for review.
Do not merge or publish a Preview release until all required gates pass.

knowledge_carried_forward: Scientific baseline v0.2.0, model artifacts, taxonomy, 42-feature contract, QC semantics and scientific gates remain unchanged.
No Qt or .NET production dependency is approved.
Qt Quick/QML is the preferred prototype candidate; WebView2 remains the current baseline pending comparative evidence.
WPF is not the primary path for a Windows/Linux/macOS product.
Full UI migration requires a separate approved architecture decision after measured prototype results.
